# Pathway: Reel · 60 s

Everything the Brain knows that applies to **Reel · 60 s**, in the order you'd use it. 304 ideas. Niche sections list only the extra, niche-specific ideas. [index](../index.md)


## Idea

- **[Hook = title + verbal + visual](../topics/hooks.md#hook-title-verbal-visual)**: Analyse every reference by its title hook, verbal hook and visual hook, plus its narrative framework and a simple outline.
- **[Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story)**: Oren's five: strong take, strong take → education, small epiphany ("Do you notice how husbands always do this?"), humour (poke fun at something), story time. Takes, small epiphanies and story time are the foundation of ~90% of content. ⚠ C3
- **[Avoid generic lists and motivation speeches](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-avoid-generic-lists)**: Oren deliberately leaves out "my top three favourite…", "three ways to…" and motivational speeches: generic content outside the frameworks won't work. ⚠ C3, C20
- **[Even "here's three things" beats no frame](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-any-framework-beats-none)**: Tristan: even a cringey "here's three things" does better than no framework; Briar lists "9 travel hacks" as a valid reach post while calling it "kind of cringe". ⚠ C20, C3
- **[Strong take, then defend or teach](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-strong-take)**: Say something is the best or the worst and defend it ("Orlando is the best sports city in North America"), or use the take as the hook and pivot to teaching. Conversation drives videos. ⚠ C7, C15
- **[Yap Map: 3–5 ideas a day](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-yap-map)**: Use dead time to log 3–5 ideas a day in a notes app from your day's touch points, personal life, media you consume and shower/workout thoughts; give each one a take.
- **[Idea faucets: Reddit and your own winners](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-reddit-faucet)**: Sort your niche subreddit by top of the month and have ChatGPT summarise what people discuss; and turn last week's most viral video into one specific buzzword ("creative tax strategies") for next week's video.
- **[Copy only true outliers](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-outliers-vs-own-average)**: A video is an outlier only against that creator's own average (20K isn't an outlier if they average 100K). Briar keeps a second TikTok account that follows only the niche; Oren's library sorts by ≥2× outliers.
- **[5 in-niche for topics, 5 outside for packaging](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-5-plus-5-creators)**: Take topics from 5 niche competitors and packaging (formats, camera angles, series) from 5 creators outside the niche; nobody knows where your combos come from. ⚠ C25
- **[You compete with the whole feed](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-compete-with-feed)**: Your rivals are everything in the viewer's feed (skits, funny and relatable people), not niche competitors; look outside your niche. Build an account that follows what your ideal viewer follows and check it 10–15 min a day for a couple of weeks. ⚠ C25
- **[Shareability: why would they send it?](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-shareability-test)**: The key test is whether someone would send it to someone else (relatable, expertise, tutorial, funny, interesting, beautiful). Our playbook ranks sends per reach as the strongest signal for reaching new people.
- **[Green or red, never grey](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-polarise-green-red)**: Take a hard stance you actually believe about 90% of the time; keep nuance for private work. People who disagree argue in the comments, which drives reach. ⚠ C7
- **[Widen the audience one layer higher](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-high-tam-one-layer-up)**: For top-of-funnel reach, widen the audience one layer ("college girls that love Pilates" → "ladies"; sales → business → money → ambition) and avoid narrowing words like "business owners", but keep a through-line to what you do. ⚠ C19
- **[Pick one goal: comments, sends or saves](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-conversation-goal)**: Decide whether a video is for comments, sends (communal language like "me and the boys after we ___") or saves; you usually can't hit all of them.
- **[Faceless works if there's a concept](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-faceless-with-concept)**: No face is needed if there is a concept: POV hands-only skits with voiceover took Gel Blaster's Mexico TikTok to 800,000. ⚠ C28
- **[AI prompt: unique, specific, observed](../topics/ai-tools.md#ideas-unique-specific-observed)**: Use AI for ideation: ask for the most unique, specific and observed situation your ideal viewer has lived. Name the problem nobody has named (Briar's "follower quality" drew "Finally, someone's talking about…"). ⚠ C22
- **[Ideas from DM and comment questions](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-questions-not-polls)**: Best ideas come from DM and comment questions, not "what should I make?" polls; ~5 people asking the same thing means thousands have it. Topic test: passionate? resonates now? most of all, will it change their actions?
- **[Community content: involve, converse, showcase](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-as-hero)**: Let the audience pick between two versions, share their wins publicly, stitch their stories (even 300-follower accounts). Three pillars: educational, conversational, social proof.
- **[14 topics, then reformat them](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-14-topics-reformatted)**: Briar's local-business tier: 14 topics for two weeks, then the same topics reformatted (green screen → whiteboard → talking head → podcast style) for the next two; weaker feedback loop.
- **[Content hackathon: make 1–2 wild pieces](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-hackathon)**: Monthly or quarterly: a safe-space kickoff, each person makes 1–2 new pieces that will crush or flop (9 a.m.–4 p.m.), presentations explaining why, team votes, the winner runs publicly. Reward innovation, not performance.
- **[Brand = intentional pairing, done consistently](../topics/brand.md#brand-intentional-pairing)**: Branding is a pairing of things; good branding is an intentional pairing of relevant things done consistently; brand is the audience's resulting association (Nike + Jordan, Harley + freedom).
- **[Decide what not to be associated with](../topics/brand.md#brand-anti-associations)**: The more important question: what do you NOT want to be associated with (collabs, podcasts, sponsors)? He'd decline even the biggest audience.
- **[Brand Journey: work backwards](../topics/brand.md#brand-journey-backwards)**: Desired outcome → what you must be known for → what you must do → what you must learn (the last gives day-one actions).
- **[Own the gap: what do you disagree with?](../topics/brand.md#brand-own-the-gap)**: Positioning = find the gap: what are creators in your space saying that you disagree with, and how can you bring a fresh perspective to old teaching?
- **[Brand story: catalyst, core truth, proof](../topics/brand.md#brand-story-catalyst-truth-proof)**: Catalyst (why it exists), core truth (what you believe that others don't, not controversy for its own sake), proof (what you do and prove over and over).
- **[Start narrow, expand in layers](../topics/brand.md#brand-start-narrow-layers)**: Early trust comes from being great at one specific thing; expand only into adjacent topics, once excellent, after consistent engagement or when the audience asks, keeping your roots. ⚠ C19
- **[80/20 interest stacking](../topics/brand.md#brand-interest-stacking)**: 80% your core subject, 20% other interests; each extra interest is another "at bat" to connect. Pillars are guidelines, not rules.
- **[Positioning: known for, shelf test](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-known-for)**: Positioning is what you're known for: not generic, remembered, AI-legible. Shelf test: stand next to everyone in the category and name your reason to exist (Monster = counterculture, Celsius = health).
- **[Positioning type and one statement](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-types)**: Pick one type (performance, category creation, counter, smart, value, niche, generational, single attribute, premium, counter-luxury, name) as north star; write "For [target] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [competitor], we [differentiator]."
- **[Brand world: characters, sets, plot](../topics/brand.md#brand-world-characters-sets)**: Map who can be on camera and every set, then plot it like TV: events, enemies (competitor moves), friends (partners to piggyback), specials (your own series for empty stretches); find the holes and refresh monthly.
- **[Events calendar: personal, culture, industry](../topics/brand.md#brand-events-calendar)**: A calendar by month or quarter of company/personal events, culture moments (New Year, summer, Black Friday) and industry events (CES, competitor launches).
- **[Brand = a title plus one emotion](../topics/brand.md#brand-title-one-emotion)**: Tombstone test: what one title would people give you, and can they attach one emotion (Nike = hard work, New Balance = style)?
- **[Counter-position = different, not opposite](../topics/brand.md#brand-counter-position-different)**: Counter-positioning means different positioning, not opposite; spike into a pocket, then grow out (Amazon with books, Vans with skaters).
- **[Small right audience beats big wrong one](../topics/brand.md#brand-follower-quality)**: How and on what you grow is what your audience will always be; 10,000 quality followers can change your life. Caleb's 68K landscape-photo followers don't engage with his current topic.
- **[Positioning: what do you replace?](../topics/brand.md#brand-what-do-you-replace)**: "You're going to need a smaller cabinet": name what you replace; and what can you do that no one else does that people care about (The Secret Footballer, Loom's "async video").
- **[Build from a belief](../topics/brand.md#brand-something-to-say)**: Build from something you believe or something you think is wrong with the world; David: counter-position and build the opposite of what you don't like.
- **[One idea beats many](../topics/brand.md#brand-one-idea)**: The strength of an idea is inversely proportional to its scope; "and" on a landing page is rarely good ("We make jeans, that's it"). ⚠ C6
- **[Three Instagram strategies](../topics/brand.md#brand-instagram-strategies)**: Expert on camera (Oren's #1, at least 3 posts/week), storytelling about an interesting business (~2/week), or extremely art-directed. People beat brand handles: personalities drive more impact. ⚠ C26, C28
- **[Content funnel: top, middle, bottom](../topics/growth.md#growth-content-funnel)**: Top of funnel gets attention and may not mention the product ("raises the floor"); middle educates about you; bottom exists to sell or sign up and gets low views.
- **[Weekly mix 4 : 2 : 1](../topics/growth.md#growth-weekly-4-2-1)**: 4 top-of-funnel high-TAM posts with a through-line, 2 middle-of-funnel "blow their mind" blueprints, 1 bottom-of-funnel "sneak peek inside" (client journey, wins, community Q&A). ⚠ C18
- **[Series get the best view-to-follower ratio](../topics/growth.md#growth-series-view-to-follower)**: Series ("day one of doing X") get the best view-to-follower ratio; days can be skipped, add value, blend in your expertise, raise the stakes, end with "follow along". Caleb: think like Netflix.
- **[70 / 20 / 10 proven, iterate, experiment](../topics/growth.md#growth-70-20-10)**: 70% proven content, 20% small iterations (new hook, CTA or format on the same subject), 10% pure experiments.
- **[Content assembly line](../topics/process.md#proc-assembly-line)**: Ideation → creation → editing per platform → distribution (post and engage) → analyse. Batching (a 12-hour day of 3–4 videos) works for some but often adds pressure that hurts performance.
- **[Six pillars of content](../topics/process.md#proc-six-pillars)**: Strategy (state the goal in one sentence), ideation, scripting, talent/energy management (teleprompter, mornings, let a yapper talk 4–8 min), editing, growth tactics.
- **[Theme first, then plan, shots, edit, copy](../topics/process.md#proc-theme-first-workflow)**: Our order: research and 3 theme options → content plan → shot list/footage audit → edit blueprint → copy pack → publishing plan → review after 24–72 h.
- **[AI for ideation, not scripting](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-ideation-not-scripting)**: Briar: AI content in 2026 has nothing to do with scripting; use it for ideas (he allows AI scripting only for local-business clients). ⚠ C22, C8
- **[Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown)**: Play another creator's popular or paid reel with its audio in a rounded card. Freeze it at each effect, shrink it to a thumbnail beside your head, explain how to make that effect, then play on. In L10 the source plays 10 times, 19.9 s of 85 s (23%), and its own lines carry the story. ⚠ C31
- **[Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank)**: Hooks as reusable fill-in templates with blanks ([X], [Y], [niche]) harvested from proven viral reels, each kept with its proof (the example reel and its views). Pick a template, fill the blanks for your niche. A third hook method next to the engineered triple hook (L01) and 'say something crazy' (L08). Adam sells the full bank as a lead magnet: '100+ Proven Viral Hook Templates'. ⚠ C34, C17

## Script

- **[Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula)**: Kallaway-style hook in three steps: context in the first words, a lean that makes the viewer want the next sentence, then a contrarian snapback that yanks them opposite to what they expect (like setting a fishing hook). He calls it the "God-tier hook formula". ⚠ C17
- **[Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words)**: Say what the video is about immediately, delivered at once by audio, visuals and on-screen text. The creator claims delaying it even to the back half of the first sentence sharply raises skip rate. ⚠ C5, C6, C24
- **[Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways)**: After the context, create curiosity with proof (a stat, number, screenshot or result), a specific pain point or benefit, or something shocking (unexpected image, statement or fact). ⚠ C12
- **[Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof)**: Back the opening claim with proof on screen in the first 2–3 s: L01 pairs "scientifically impossible to skip" with a retention graph; L03 shows ROBOT vs PRO animations side by side. ⚠ C7
- **[No intro: topic and number first](../topics/hooks.md#hook-no-intro-payoff-first)**: Rahul never greets: the topic and a number (price, score, date) are spoken and on screen in the first 1–2 s. Our playbook: open on the most striking frame plus a hook text of 8 words or fewer; no logos, no slow intros.
- **[Hook window: 2–3 s short, 15–20 s long](../topics/hooks.md#hook-window-short-vs-long)**: Short form gives about 2–3 s to win attention. YouTube long form: about 15–20 s max (the industry says 30 s); the viewer checks it is what they clicked and the right person to hear it from.
- **[Contrarian statement or "don't buy X"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrarian-statement)**: Say something most people believe is false and offer the alternative ("Subscribers, views, likes don't matter…"). Rahul's versions: "Don't buy the RTX 5070", "8 GB GPU in 2026 is a waste of money", "stop paying ₹8,000 a year for Photoshop". ⚠ C7, C15
- **[Unexpected-fact hooks are wearing thin](../topics/hooks.md#hook-unexpected-facts-tiresome)**: Caleb (Feb 2025) allows unexpected-fact hooks but says they are "getting a little tiresome"; he prefers bold contrarian statements. ⚠ C12
- **[Pattern-interrupt opener](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pattern-interrupt)**: Open on something odd that breaks the scroll, e.g. Gary Vee's "I eat blueberries like it's my job... You missed the first 30 I ate", one of the most viral clips Caleb made.
- **[Question on a pain point](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pain-question)**: Open with a question about the viewer's pain: "Does your animation look robotic?", "Why do your Claude edits look pro but sound like a silent movie?". Caleb calls a thought-provoking question a "thumbs stopper".
- **[Contrast hook: looks X, sounds Y](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrast-looks-sounds)**: Two-part contrast on screen: "Looks pro. Sounds like this: 🔇". Sets up the problem in one glance.
- **["You've probably seen X lately…"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-trend-riding)**: Ride a trend the viewer has already noticed, then promise the how: "You've probably seen these videos lately where people are editing with Claude or ChatGPT. Let me show you how."
- **["Do this now": a tiny effort, instant payoff](../topics/hooks.md#hook-do-this-now)**: The viewer can test it while watching: "put your phone on airplane mode… the code is still changing", or "Aapko pata hai…" change one word in the Gmail URL. The Gmail trick was Rahul's best organic reel at 2.38× followers.
- **[Hyper-local conditional hook](../topics/hooks.md#hook-hyper-local-conditional)**: Call out a specific place and moment: "If you're going to Nehru Place or Lamington Road this weekend to build a PC, listen before you enter the shop…", with real market names as road-sign graphics. ⚠ C19
- **[Sarcastic or date-stamped mockery opener](../topics/hooks.md#hook-sarcastic-opener)**: Open with mockery tied to a date or price ("Thinking of a ₹1 lakh PC in October 2026? The shopkeeper will laugh at you") or sarcastic congratulations ("Wow, congratulations! ₹75,000… your first PC").
- **[One Mississippi: understood in 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#hook-one-mississippi)**: If a line takes longer than about 2 seconds to understand it fails; for a passer-by it must be instant. Yet Harry also says that if everyone gets it you may be doing something wrong: being texted to a friend as "What is this?" is fine. ⚠ C5
- **[First line only sells the second](../topics/hooks.md#hook-first-line-second-line)**: The job of the first line is to get the second line read ("What's going on?"), via Dave Gerhardt from Joe Sugarman.
- **[Don't overthink: say something crazy](../topics/hooks.md#hook-say-something-crazy)**: Briar's hook philosophy: don't think about hooks too much; say something crazy and get into it. He also says a great hook is harder to teach. ⚠ C17
- **[Hook, problem, journey, lesson, CTA](../topics/story.md#story-hook-problem-journey-lesson-cta)**: Caleb's flexible story frame: hook, specific relatable stakes, the journey with its low points and messy middle (progress, not perfection), a usable lesson in chunked steps, then a call to action. Rules can be broken.
- **[Story types: origin, failure, success, client](../topics/story.md#story-origin-retell)**: Origin stories resonate most, so keep retelling them (every post meets a cold audience). Failure stories with the lesson build trust (losses are more relatable than wins; don't be a robot). Success, before/after and client wins are the proof.
- **[Industry trope, then your contrary view](../topics/story.md#story-industry-contrarian)**: State the industry trope, then your contrary belief, respectfully and without naming names ("never tell your audience about your offer in your organic content"). ⚠ C15
- **[Script: hook → story → 2 points](../topics/story.md#story-hook-story-two-points)**: Hook ("Kick Coffee is the best coffee shop in Newport Beach"), a real anecdote, then your two reasons.
- **["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile)**: After the hook, call out the opposite argument and disprove it, then make your point; it removes objections up front and keeps people watching.
- **[4 or 5 mini takes](../topics/story.md#story-4-5-things)**: "Observations I made at Coachella as a brand strategist": 4–5 mini videos in one, each a strong take; people stay for the next one. ⚠ C3, C20
- **[Conflict and a shared enemy](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-everywhere)**: Build every example on conflict: before/after, problem/solution, an enemy (A = approach, B = belief, C = competitor), juxtaposition. Tristan: a shared enemy is one of the best copywriting principles.
- **[Hinge stories on "but"](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-via-but)**: Tell a story around the word "but" without writing it: what went wrong next (woke 8:52, mum blocks the door over blue shorts…) instead of "I got on the train, had a coffee".
- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)**: Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Open loops, re-open one at ~15 s](../topics/story.md#story-open-loops)**: Open curiosity at the start and keep opening loops with illustrations, metaphors and stats. Viewers who got the point 15 s in leave, so re-open a new loop around 15 s; a spoken "Why?" works. Caleb wants editors who "open and close loops".
- **[Statement, reason, re-hook, "Why?", payoff](../topics/story.md#story-live-hook-build)**: Briar's live script: strong statement, a one-sentence reason (so people aren't annoyed), a stronger re-hook with high stakes, "Why?" to open the next loop, the payoff, then a wild closing line as a comment driver.
- **[Promise a numbered list or a download](../topics/story.md#story-promised-list-open-loop)**: A numbered promise ("5 frameworks") or a companion download promised throughout keeps an open loop across a long video.
- **[Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline)**: Simple outline Oren uses all the time: controversial question → rapid-fire opinions → justifications → punchline. Reliable mechanisms: "blitz" rapid-fire lists ("10 out of 10 niche habits…") and storytime. ⚠ C3
- **[Structure = dividing lines + parallelism](../topics/story.md#story-dividing-lines-parallelism)**: Split the piece into clear parts with matching headings (first 100 readers / next 9,900) so it's cohesive. David adds the 1971 paper "That's Interesting": show two things thought different are one, or one thing is two.
- **[State an honest limitation](../topics/story.md#story-honest-limitation)**: "The honest part: it only ships 78 sounds." Admitting a limit makes the rest believable.
- **[Answer objections inside the content](../topics/story.md#story-answer-objections)**: Mine comments (and sales calls) for recurring objections and answer them in future content, like a video sales letter; Oren summarises call objections weekly and feeds them back into content.
- **[Every word not working works against you](../topics/text.md#text-kaplans-law)**: Kaplan's Law of Words; pull-out test: if a sentence can be removed and the paragraph still works, cut it; a paragraph is a burrito that shouldn't come apart in the air.
- **[Visualize, falsify, nobody else can say it](../topics/text.md#text-three-rules)**: Run every line through three questions: can I visualize it, can I falsify it, can nobody else say it? Three no's = rubbish; three yes's = onto something.
- **[Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete)**: Rewrite down an abstract → concrete ladder until you hit an object (regain fitness → Couch to 5K) and swap literal words for visual ones ("1,000 songs in your pocket", not "media player").
- **[Point, don't talk; give me a fact](../topics/text.md#text-point-dont-talk)**: Swap adjectives for pointable facts ("Looks like Ryan Gosling, 6'2"" beats "smart, funny"). If in doubt, give a fact, then build on it (Heinz bottles refilled → "Even when it's not Heinz, it's Heinz").
- **[Small, sincere, believable claims](../topics/text.md#text-small-sincere-claim)**: David on Harry's ad: it's not a big claim, so it's believable and sincere; the art of simple communication. ⚠ C7
- **[Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known)**: Make a product make sense by comparing it to products people know: "Tougher than an F-150, faster than a 911" (concrete word, shorter, parallel).
- **[Copy devices: time frames, reframes, alliteration](../topics/text.md#text-expand-time-frame)**: Expand the time frame (22,000 career hours vs 4 a day), reframe a cost as a saving, tweak numbers for parallelism (22,000 / 2), and pair alliteration with a contradiction ("The dating app designed to be deleted").
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)**: Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Four copy styles](../topics/text.md#text-four-copy-styles)**: Direct response (urgent, numbers, confrontational; Oren's "highest efficacy"), evidence-led (testimonials, calm), human/story-driven, culturally savvy (pop-culture wordplay).
- **[Tell the story, don't claim the trait](../topics/brand.md#brand-tell-story-not-trait)**: Your story is the differentiator: the ~32-hour editing stretch instead of "I'm a hard worker"; Bezos' door desk instead of "resourceful".
- **[Say what no competitor could sign](../topics/brand.md#brand-copy-cant-be-copied)**: "Never write an ad a competitor can sign": say what only you can say (New Balance: "Worn by supermodels in London and dads in Ohio").
- **[Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta)**: "Comment 'hooks' and I'll send it to you": a comment-to-DM freebie, with social proof (700K views) raising its value. Rahul uses it on nearly every reel with the keyword in the caption and as a big yellow label in the last 2–4 s. ⚠ C1, C10, C18, C23
- **[Anti-CTA: no DM needed, it's all here](../topics/growth.md#growth-anti-cta)**: "No DM for resources, everything you need is right here": stands out against everyone's comment-to-DM CTA and builds trust and saves. ⚠ C1, C23
- **[CTA that doesn't sell: your takeaway](../topics/growth.md#growth-takeaway-cta)**: A CTA just tells people to act: "comment your biggest takeaway and how you'll apply it" drives engagement and commitment. Caleb says the best content isn't pushing and selling. ⚠ C10
- **[Share CTA: send it to your team](../topics/growth.md#growth-share-cta)**: Caleb closes his course asking viewers to send it to their team on Slack or text it to a friend; our caption rules prefer "send this to…" or "save for your next…".
- **[Seed + reference layout → many rewrites](../topics/process.md#proc-seed-reference-rewrites)**: Harry's ad: a seed line, a conflict list, a borrowed reference layout, 2 days and 25 rewrites, spitballing without judging (let the dirty tap water run clean), feedback from people with taste, then a design pass.
- **[Write 4–5 versions side by side](../topics/process.md#proc-four-five-versions)**: Write several versions for freedom to be wrong; showing three versions gets far better feedback than one ("use that sentence, but put it in that one").
- **[Draft in the final tool, judge in context](../topics/process.md#proc-write-in-final-tool)**: Write the newsletter in ConvertKit and ads in Figma as readers will see them; test a billboard among seven other ads with people walking by.
- **[Who, what to say, how to say it](../topics/process.md#proc-who-say-how)**: Copywriting's three pieces: who you're talking to (and what they're doing then), having something to say, saying it well; move them from current to desired attitude.
- **[Brand project plus a human layer](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-brand-project-human-layer)**: Upload the positioning statement, product info, site copy and testimonials (not big brand guides) to a shared project, give feedback, then add human case studies and nuances on top.
- **[Storyboard table before any edit](../topics/process.md#l10-storyboard-before-edit)**: Before Claude touches the footage (he does it even before shooting), it writes the whole video as a table: every line, what is on screen, which tool makes it. You fix the plan and agree on it, then Claude builds the edit from it. Chandler's columns: # / Freeze (time) / Chandler says / On screen. ⚠ C30
- **[SCORE and EMPHASIS lines per beat](../topics/sound.md#l10-storyboard-score-emphasis)**: The source creator's storyboard ("claude-editing / storyboard, v2, 24 beats") gives each beat timecodes, duration, shot type, the spoken line, a direction, an EMPHASIS line (which word goes gold serif, which is struck through) and a SCORE line with music cues such as "drop 1 on 'Claude did.'" and "tape stop under the scratch 0:28.3, drop 2 on 'storyboard'".
- **[Undercut a paid course in the hook](../topics/hooks.md#l10-undercut-paid-hook)**: Open with the rival's strongest line ("I didn't edit a single second of this video. Claude did."), then undercut its price: "This guy's selling this for 97 bucks. I'm giving it away for free." A $97 checkout card pops on the source as he says it. ⚠ C11, C1
- **[Expertise hook: years of niche in 60 seconds](../topics/hooks.md#l11-expertise-hook)**: Template: "[N years] of [niche] in [60 seconds]". A big time investment, the topic and a tiny time cost in one line: authority without saying 'I'm an expert', plus a compression promise (my years, your minute). Context and lean land together. Reel's example: "3 years of therapy in 60 seconds" (on-screen '3 years of Therapy in 1 minute', pill 40.5M). ⚠ C7
- **[Warning hook: never start X without these N things](../topics/hooks.md#l11-warning-hook)**: Template: "Never start a [X] if you don't have these [Y] things". A prohibition on a big action the viewer is considering, gated by a counted checklist. Loss aversion plus an open loop (which things? do I have them?); unlike a pure 'don't buy X' debunk it ends with something useful. Reel's example: "Never start a business if you don't have these 4 things" (number tiles 1-2-3-4, red '4 THINGS', pill 339K). ⚠ C15
- **[Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook)**: Template: "This is exactly what you want to see when you're [situation]". 'This' points at a visual of the ideal outcome; the situation lets the right viewer self-select. The spoken context arrives at the end of the sentence, so the visual must carry it from frame 1. Reel's example: "This is exactly what you want to see when you're buying an industrial prop[erty]" over an aerial warehouse shot with a map pin (pill 3.6M). ⚠ C35
- **[Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook)**: Template: "If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]". A tiny repeatable habit, 'every single day', then three concrete outcomes (rule of three). Each outcome is another reason to care. Reel's example: "If you take creatine every single day, you're going to build more muscle, recover faster, and get way more out of all the hard work that you're putting in in the gym" (pill 28M, the reel's biggest example). ⚠ C7
- **[Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates)**: The three classic templates spelled out: Challenge "I'm going to [X] for [Y] days straight" (example: study 8 hours, 5 days straight, 4.9M); Ranking "Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]" (example: rating supplements so you don't waste your money, S–F tier board, 4.7M); List "These are the 5 best ways to use [X]" (example: sound effects, 1.9M). Each carries a hard number or names what the viewer saves. ⚠ C3, C20

## Film

- **[Comment farm: plant an odd detail](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-comment-farm)**: Plant something odd in frame that people will comment on (an open Birkin bag on a NYC walk, a visible laptop tab, a bag on a car roof), or ride a hot news topic and tie it to your niche.
- **[Formats working in Dec 2025](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-green-screen-beginners)**: Briar: green screen with one image behind you for beginners; the clone format (talking to yourself) about to be overplayed; livestreams for educators as a "baked-in webinar".
- **[Voice cadence as pattern interrupt](../topics/sound.md#sound-voice-cadence-interrupt)**: Changing cadence (fast/slow, loud/soft) works as a pattern interrupt; even a monotone voice can become "your bit".
- **[Dark matte background, warm key, gold rim](../topics/colour.md#colour-dark-matte-warm-key)**: L01's look: dark matte background, warm key light on the face, gold rim light.
- **[Yap types: standard, walking, car](../topics/filming.md#film-yap-formats)**: The simplest creator format, phone on a tripod: standard yap (sitting), walking yap (FaceTime-with-a-friend feel, not for beginners), car yap (candid). "The key to the yap is you just do it."
- **[Frame low, leave headroom for graphics](../topics/filming.md#film-framed-graphic-headroom)**: Framed graphic yap: frame yourself low with space above your head for a graphic; plan head, caption and graphic placement and keep graphics vertical.
- **[Tripod + Bluetooth remote + plug-in mic](../topics/filming.md#film-yap-gear)**: iPhone on a ~$50 tripod with extending legs and a Bluetooth remote, plus a Røde USB-C plug-in mic or wired EarPods. AirPods do not work.
- **[Pause in silence to think](../topics/filming.md#film-recut-pause-method)**: Whenever you need to think, stop and stay silent with eye contact, then talk again; remove silences later (ReCut or silence removal). A 6–7 min raw clip is fine.
- **[Re-record the intro at the end](../topics/filming.md#film-redo-intro-at-end)**: The intro matters most but is where you're most awkward; after ~3 minutes you're in flow, so record the intro again then.
- **[Treat places as sets](../topics/filming.md#film-sets-evergreen-temporary)**: Evergreen sets (office corner, warehouse, studio day) and temporary ones (a booth the night before). Oren's course rotates 6 physical sets every few minutes as pattern interrupts.
- **[Talking-head light and lens looks](../topics/filming.md#film-talking-head-lighting)**: Soft key front-left with a 35–50 mm wide-aperture look (L06); warm key with gold rim (L01); 20–24 mm wide for energy (L07); high-key soft 3-point with rim for a podcast (L08).
- **[Talk to a photo of your best friend](../topics/filming.md#film-best-friend-behind-camera)**: For camera nerves: prep fully then let go (The Inner Game of Tennis), and put a printed photo of your best friend behind the camera; decide later whether to post.
- **[Sacred hour at your best energy](../topics/filming.md#film-sacred-hour)**: Block one fixed hour a day to record (Briar), at your best time of day (Caleb: mornings), and protect it like an important meeting.
- **[Nods and thumbs-up from behind camera](../topics/filming.md#film-on-set-feedback)**: The videographer nods (more intensely as the point gets better) and gives a thumbs up; fist bump between takes naming 1–2 specific things; message the talent 15–20 min after the shoot.
- **[TikTok: more candid, shot on iPhone](../topics/filming.md#film-tiktok-candid-iphone)**: Oren's per-network strategy makes TikTok content more personal and candid, shot on iPhone. ⚠ C27
- **[iPhone 15: frame rates, modes, HDR](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-frame-rates)**: 4K 30 default; 4K 60 for reps you'll slow; 4K 24 for travel; 240 fps slo-mo for single moments; Action mode handheld; Cinematic mode for B-roll; HDR Video off for heavy grading (no Log/ProRes on the base 15).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)**: The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Lock AE/AF, grid on, clean lens](../topics/filming.md#film-lock-ae-af)**: Long-press to lock exposure and focus, then drop exposure 0.3–0.7 to save highlights; Grid and Level on; clean the lens before every shoot; 48 MP photos for landscapes you'll crop.
- **[Solo: record, then walk in](../topics/filming.md#film-solo-start)**: Start recording and walk into frame (trim later), or use the 3 s/10 s timer; a watch or Bluetooth remote is faster.
- **[Fixed set and colour identity](../topics/brand.md#brand-fixed-set-identity)**: Rahul's set never changes (purple/blue wash, warm lamp, mic on an arm) with a yellow accent; he talks straight to lens, sarcastic ("Come on Intel") with lots of gestures, recognisable at thumbnail size.

## Edit

- **[Something new on screen every 1.2–2.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-change-every-1-5-2-5s)**: Change something (cut, layout swap, label, card, animation) every 1.5–2.5 s (L01, L02). Rahul measured at roughly every 1.2–2 s in every reel; his sponsored Flipkart reel was the fastest at 1.2 s. ⚠ C6, C13, C21
- **[Graphic yap: one overlay every ~2 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-graphic-yap-overlay-2s)**: Chaotic graphic yap: overlay camera-roll images or clips about one every 2 s, so a 60 s video needs about 30 images. A full-screen version cuts 9:16 Canva images over the talking.
- **[Sell a long video with a hyper-edited teaser](../topics/editing.md#edit-teaser-hyper-edited)**: L08's 46 s teaser of its single most contrarian soundbite: shots 0.8–1.8 s, 10–15% push-ins/outs, screen flashes, speed ramps on percussive hits, bass drops on text pops, ending on a metallic thud and hard cut to black.
- **[Train a cut rhythm, then break it](../topics/editing.md#edit-trained-rhythm-break)**: A regular cut cadence (Caleb's example: 12 frames / 36 frames) trains the viewer; breaking the pattern then emphasises the big moment.
- **[Axial jump cuts every 3–6 words](../topics/editing.md#edit-axial-jump-cuts)**: Talking head: cut from the medium shot to a digital punch-in on the same angle every 3–6 words to hit emphasis words.
- **[Cut every breath and pause](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-breaths-no-dead-air)**: Jump cuts remove breaths (the ReCut method in action). Rahul's reels have no dead air: under 2.5% of 100 ms windows sit 25 dB below the median level.
- **[Speed ramps: dead time, beats, top rep](../topics/editing.md#edit-speed-ramps)**: Subtle ramps on browser scrolls and screen recordings remove dead time (L07); the L08 teaser syncs ramps to percussive hits; our gym default ramps into the top rep.
- **[Split layouts: graphic plus face](../topics/editing.md#edit-split-screen-graphic-face)**: Graphic on top, face below, switching to full face for key lines (L01); Rahul's animated top ~55% over a face cam; L04's red step board under the face; long-form: 9:16 examples in rounded windows on the left ~40%, speaker on the right (L06).
- **[Switch layouts every few seconds](../topics/editing.md#edit-layout-switching)**: Rahul's organic reels switch between full-frame talking head with pop-up labels, screen/card with circular face cam, and 1–3 s meme cutaways every few seconds instead of holding one layout.
- **[Screen content with a circular face cam](../topics/editing.md#edit-screen-card-circle-facecam)**: Screen recordings fill the frame with a circular face cam: Rahul bottom-centre with a yellow ring and an app-logo badge; Oren in dark rounded cards with drop shadows plus a floating circular PiP camera.
- **[Meme cutaways with the product pasted in](../topics/editing.md#edit-meme-cutaways)**: 1–3 s full-screen meme cutaways (Bollywood, Joker, DiCaprio, Messi) with the price or product composited in; often reused as the cover.
- **[Show proof on screen](../topics/editing.md#edit-proof-inserts)**: Rahul inserts article, doc and GitHub screenshots with yellow highlighter on the key line; Oren runs live tool walkthroughs as proof.
- **[Cut on the beat or on motion](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-on-beat-motion)**: Our edit blueprint sets cut rules (on the beat or on motion) and travel uses a wide → close-up rhythm. Khandala cut every 1.5 s, which lands on 80 and 120 BPM beats (2 or 3 beats per shot), so music could be added later.
- **[Length: 7–15 s vibe, 20–60 s value](../topics/editing.md#edit-length-by-type)**: 7–15 s for pure vibe/viral reels (completion + loops), 20–60 s for tutorials and vlogs with value, under 3 min to stay eligible for non-follower recommendation.
- **[Cull near-duplicates; keep the strongest](../topics/editing.md#edit-cull-near-duplicates)**: Khandala: 43 raw files to 1 reel + 1 carousel; dropped near-duplicates, tilted horizons, soft digital zooms, litter in frame and harsh midday light that broke the sunset look.
- **[Face check before using any frame](../topics/editing.md#edit-face-check)**: Never use frames where the mouth is open or mid-word, the tongue shows, eyes are mid-blink or the angle is awkward; prefer a clear smile, a confident neutral or a candid look-away. The Khandala profile shot was replaced after this feedback.
- **[Which app for which job](../topics/editing.md#edit-app-roles)**: Our defaults: CapCut for heavy edits and grading, VN for precise timeline and keyframes, Edits for final assembly, trending audio and direct posting (Edits exports have no watermark).
- **[Subtle 105–110% punch-in on key phrases](../topics/effects.md#fx-subtle-punch-in)**: Subtle 105–110% punch-ins on key phrases and when each numbered section starts (L06); Rahul punches in on emphasis.
- **[Bigger 1.15–1.3× punch-ins on punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-big-punch-in)**: Smooth 1.15–1.3× punch-ins on punchlines and framework declarations, bigger than L06's.
- **[B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline)**: Desaturate and hold the frame on a sarcastic line.
- **[Hard cuts; motion only on overlays](../topics/transitions.md#tr-hard-cuts-motion-on-overlays)**: Jump cuts are hard cuts; the movement lives in the overlay windows that slide in with spring/ease-out.
- **[Horizontal wipes and slide-ins](../topics/transitions.md#tr-kinetic-wipes)**: Kinetic text slide-ins and horizontal wipes move between ideas, each with a whoosh.
- **[End on a thud and cut to black](../topics/transitions.md#tr-cut-to-black-thud)**: The teaser ends on a metallic thud and a hard cut to black.
- **[Zoom/pan the board to each step](../topics/transitions.md#tr-board-zoom-to-step)**: A step board zooms/pans to each step, then pulls back to the whole board (the full map in one frame) at the end.
- **[Warm golden mids, soft highlights](../topics/colour.md#colour-warm-golden-mids)**: Oren's yapping guide: warm, golden midtones with slightly desaturated highlights.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)**: Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **["Take a picture" save moment](../topics/growth.md#growth-screenshot-save-moment)**: "I'll leave it here for a second so you can take a picture", then pull back to the full map in one frame at the end: save bait.
- **[Waterfall and repurpose winners](../topics/growth.md#growth-waterfall)**: Mine one long piece into 10+ (clips, quotes, a written post reused as a reel caption, carousels), and use a winner on one platform to seed others (tweet → short → printed poster → LinkedIn → YouTube).
- **[Edit blueprint per video](../topics/process.md#proc-edit-blueprint)**: Our template: theme, format and length, audio, 0–2 s hook, timestamped timeline, cut rules, text, grade, sound design, cover frame, export, app steps.
- **[Reference-driven AI editing](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-reference-driven-edit)**: Give Claude the reel whose style you like, then your raw footage path; it edits in that style with no timeline editor; then give feedback in plain words. ⚠ C8, C22
- **[Turn the workflow into a skill](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-turn-into-skill)**: "Hey, turn this into a skill": next time it's one prompt. Oren's levels: chat → project → skills → agents → a "true brain"; repeatable things become skills, with one owner per skill.
- **[Seven-repo editing stack](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-seven-tool-stack)**: FFmpeg (every cut, mix, render), faster-whisper (word timing), Whisper, yt-dlp (download sources), OpenCV + contrib CSRT tracker (follow the speaker in a 9:16 crop), Puppeteer (render HTML captions), HyperFrames (agent-built motion graphics).
- **[Word-level transcription for captions and cuts](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-word-level-transcription)**: faster-whisper gives word timestamps, so every cut and word-by-word caption can be placed against the words.
- **[Demo each effect on your own shot](../topics/effects.md#l10-apply-effect-on-yourself)**: Each technique is applied to his own footage as he names it: grade-panel sliders move and his saturation measurably drops (SATAVG ~8 to ~4.5 at 56 s), his shot shrinks into the centre of the 3x3 wall, the words go behind his head. It works as proof and as a pattern interrupt.
- **[Plain shadowed captions, no box](../topics/text.md#l10-plain-shadow-captions)**: Captions as plain white bold sans (SF Pro/Inter-like) with a soft drop shadow and no background box, 1-3 words, centred at ~61% height just above the laptop edge. He calls it cleaner than the source's green box. ⚠ C29
- **[Before/after slider reveals the grade](../topics/effects.md#l10-grade-slider-reveal)**: The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.
- **[Whip pan over recursive zoom](../topics/transitions.md#l10-whip-not-recursive-zoom)**: He skips the source's recursive zoom ("shrink the shot into a picture of itself, 3 levels deep, then push through it with a spin and blur") as "a bit too much" and uses a whip pan, which "looks cleaner". Measured: about 5 frames of horizontal motion blur into a new framing, with a whoosh and a hit.
- **[Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example)**: Each item = a template card (~2–3 s: numbered badge, the template typing on with blanks in yellow) followed by a real viral reel that used it (~2–3.5 s, full-frame with its own audio and a view-count pill). 7 pairs in 49.6 s; 48% of the runtime is other creators' clips. ⚠ C31

## Sound

- **[A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event)**: An edit without SFX feels like a "silent movie": put a pop, click, whoosh or snap on every visual change. ⚠ C13, C21
- **[SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map)**: Whoosh for movement (slides, wipes, push-ins, window slide-ins), pop for text in, chime for a green check, thud or click for impact or a card change.
- **[Quiet music bed near −22 to −24 dB](../topics/sound.md#sound-quiet-bed-throughout)**: A low ambient synth (L01) or lo-fi/chill-hop (L06) bed runs under the whole video; Oren's sits at about −22 to −24 dB under the voice, with SFX on top.
- **[Keyboard clicks and UI pops on bullets](../topics/sound.md#sound-ui-clicks-bullets)**: UI clicks on screen recordings (L06); mechanical keyboard clicks, UI bubble pops and switch clicks on bullets and badges (L07).
- **[Chapter sounds: risers, booms, set foley](../topics/sound.md#sound-riser-sub-boom-chapters)**: Risers and sub-boom impacts at chapter starts and ends; CRT degauss/static on chapter cards; marker squeaks during whiteboard segments.
- **[Bass hit on every key text pop](../topics/sound.md#sound-bass-hit-text-pop)**: The L08 teaser lands impacts/bass drops on key text pops ("$100,000/MONTH", "WHY") and a metallic thud before the cut to black.
- **[Music changes by section](../topics/sound.md#sound-music-by-section)**: Driving synthwave with sub-bass for the hook, lo-fi under teaching, deep house for tactics, then an emotional swell into a clean cut at the outro; L06's music also rises at the outro.
- **[Broadcast voice: compress, de-ess, high-pass](../topics/sound.md#sound-broadcast-voice-chain)**: Close mic, tight compression, heavy de-essing, high-pass filter, air boost around 10–12 kHz, proximity low end, room reverb removed.
- **[Mix measured at −14 LUFS](../topics/sound.md#sound-loudness-minus-14)**: All 12 Rahul reels measured −14 LUFS with a 2.2–4.8 LU range (heavily compressed). The quietest 5% sits 9–21 dB under speech, never silent, pointing to a constant low bed (inferred).
- **[Trending audio only when it fits](../topics/sound.md#sound-trending-audio-fit)**: Trending audio boosts discovery when it fits the format: energetic for gym transformations, nostalgic acoustic for travel recaps, spoken for skits; original voice-over builds connection.
- **[Free SFX from Openverse, CC0 only](../topics/sound.md#sound-openverse-cc0)**: Openverse searches millions of openly licensed sounds with no API key; use CC0 for Instagram; CC-BY needs credit in the caption.
- **[AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement)**: AI editors can't hear. Real SFX places a real recording on each moment, ducks it under voice and outputs MP4 + WAV + report (only 78 UI sounds, so pair it with a library); earshot critiques the mix and sync and makes whooshes in code.
- **[Half-second music dropout after the punchline](../topics/sound.md#l10-dropout-after-punchline)**: Right after the hook line "Claude did." the whole mix drops to near-silence (-42 LUFS) for about 0.5 s at 2.50 s, then the beat returns. The rest of the 85 s has no silence at all.

## Graphics

- **[Entrances ease out, exits ease in](../topics/effects.md#fx-ease-out-entrances)**: Things that arrive ease out (fast, then a long brake, "as if set down by a steady hand"); things that leave ease in (slow start, then away). Oren's overlays slide in with spring/ease-out. ⚠ C2
- **[UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui)**: Interface elements and text pops use a spring that overshoots its target a little, then settles (spring/bounce slide-ins in L02; spring UI cards in L07).
- **[Nothing linear](../topics/effects.md#fx-nothing-linear)**: Nothing in the real world moves at constant speed; linear motion starts and stops all at once and looks robotic. ⚠ C2
- **[Make motion visible with a dotted trail](../topics/effects.md#fx-trail-visual-proof)**: The easing tutorial has no cuts: a position-vs-time graph animates continuously with a dotted trail (evenly spaced = linear, bunched = eased) while caption words change every ~0.3–0.5 s.
- **[Animated number counters](../topics/effects.md#fx-number-counter)**: Numbers count up on screen (5,220,123 sounds, GitHub stars ticking; Rahul's odometer ₹ counter and an opening price ticker counting to ₹75,000).
- **[n/3 progress badges in list videos](../topics/effects.md#fx-progress-badges)**: Numbered 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges mark each item in a list video and hold attention.
- **[Frosted cards, drawn diagrams, red arrows](../topics/effects.md#fx-frosted-glass-cards)**: Frosted-glass UI cards (L01, L02), drawn diagrams (curves, radar, fishing line) and red circles/arrows that guide the eye (L01).
- **[Price strikes, stamps, pills and ticks](../topics/effects.md#fx-price-strike-through)**: Strike through the old price then show the new; a red "DON'T BUY" stamp; green "₹60,000 SAVED" and "FREE" pills; ticks filling a checklist.
- **[Kinetic type: float-ins, glow, pop-ins](../topics/effects.md#fx-kinetic-words)**: Spoken keywords float in as kinetic text (L07); the L08 teaser adds outer glow, chromatic aberration, scale pop-ins and tracked floating text with cubic-bezier easing.
- **[Teaching text: clean sans, red/green](../topics/text.md#text-clean-sans-teaching)**: Clean sans (Inter / SF Pro style), white and yellow on dark; red = bad/wrong (or price up), green = good/right (or saved).
- **[Serif italic emphasis + sans body](../topics/text.md#text-serif-italic-emphasis)**: Emphasis words in serif italic (*pro*, *honest*), body in clean sans, keyword highlights in yellow/orange. Our Khandala reel used Instrument Serif Italic.
- **[Yellow bold serif section titles](../topics/text.md#text-yellow-serif-section-titles)**: Section title cards in a yellow bold serif (Garamond/Cheltenham-like) with shadow/outline, paired with clean sans UI.
- **[Extended bold sans titles, neon highlights](../topics/text.md#text-extended-sans-neon)**: Extended bold geometric sans titles (Druk Wide / Monument Extended style) + Inter/Neue Haas body; white on dark with cyan, lime and neon-pink highlights on numbers and acronyms.
- **[Script + heavy extruded sans pairing](../topics/text.md#text-script-plus-heavy-sans)**: Teaser pairing of a brush script with a heavy extruded/condensed bold sans (Futura Bold / Montserrat ExtraBold-like); palette red #FF0033, cyan #00CCFF, white, charcoal.
- **[Word-by-word captions, key word highlighted](../topics/text.md#text-word-by-word-highlight)**: One word or phrase at a time; the key word sits in a coloured highlight box (red box in L03, yellow or a selection box in Rahul's Layout A).
- **[Uppercase caption bar between halves](../topics/text.md#text-uppercase-caption-bar)**: Uppercase bold white caption bar placed between the two split-screen halves, 3–4 words at a time.
- **[Yellow caps labels and big ₹ figures](../topics/text.md#text-yellow-condensed-labels)**: Heavy condensed all-caps yellow labels of 1–3 words on a black box ("WI-FI OFF"), large yellow ₹ figures with a drop shadow, and receipt-style or dark UI data cards that look like real documents.
- **[Captions on yaps for almost everybody](../topics/text.md#text-captions-on-yaps)**: Oren recommends captions and a title on talk-to-camera videos "for almost everybody" (both "really important"); a standard yap can work without. His own long-form has no burned-in captions. ⚠ C4
- **[Keep text out of the UI zones](../topics/text.md#text-safe-zone)**: Reels are 9:16 1080×1920; keep text away from the top ~250 px, bottom ~350 px and the right-side button rail.
- **[One element can carry it](../topics/text.md#text-one-element)**: Neil French: ads are thought to need header, subheader, picture and logo; if one element does it, you're onto a winner. "It doesn't look like an ad, so you read it." ⚠ C6
- **[Covers: payoff frame, number, face, accent](../topics/text.md#text-cover-meme-payoff)**: Rahul's meme covers come from the reel's own payoff frame, so the cover promises the ending; covers carry a ₹ number or score, a face and yellow accent. Our playbook keeps one cover style per pillar.
- **[Near-black with one accent colour](../topics/colour.md#colour-near-black-one-accent)**: The easing tutorial is near-black with a red glow, red as the only accent; Rahul uses yellow (≈ #F5B800) on black as his single brand accent everywhere.
- **[Fit the tone; make them feel smart](../topics/brand.md#brand-tone-fit)**: Harry removed Hinge's mascot because Hinge isn't silly (Duolingo is). And if customers feel smart choosing you ("brains instead of wealth"), you did something right.
- **[Show the comment → DM funnel on screen](../topics/growth.md#growth-show-the-funnel)**: The ending shows a mock comment box with the keyword being typed, then a DM preview with the freebie; Rahul's freebies are living resources (live-price part lists, tier list, checklist), not a repeat of the video.
- **[Copy and design are one](../topics/process.md#proc-copy-design-one)**: Harry can't separate copy and design: fit key lines on one line, bold the rhythm words ("twice", "both") in a design pass, and make illustrations match the story (the money-thrower looks annoyed).
- **[The four-line easing prompt](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-easing-prompt)**: Tell the AI building motion graphics: "Entrances: ease out. Exits: ease in. Interface: spring, slight overshoot. Nothing linear." ⚠ C2
- **[Text behind your head](../topics/effects.md#l10-text-behind-head)**: Cut the speaker out with a person-segmentation model and put words on a layer between the background and the person, so the title sits behind the head. He uses it for the topic title, his brand name ("Chandler Intelligence", two-tone) and the CTA keyword "EDIT" (huge, outlined, low opacity).
- **[Real screenshot beats an AI mock-up](../topics/editing.md#l10-real-screenshot-not-mockup)**: For UI graphics such as an editor timeline, a real screenshot looks better than a generated mock-up. He shows both, back to back.
- **[3x3 wall of reels proves a trend](../topics/effects.md#l10-3x3-reel-wall)**: To show that "lots of people are doing this", his shot shrinks into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid and 8 downloaded reels pop in around it, one per frame. The grid then stays on as the thumbnail. ⚠ C31
- **[View-count pill on every example](../topics/effects.md#l11-view-count-proof-pill)**: A dark rounded pill with an eye icon and the example's views (40.5M, 339K, 4.9M, 4.7M, 1.9M, 3.6M, 28M) sits lower-centre on every borrowed clip, so each claim arrives with proof. The numbers are the creator's overlay, not verified.
- **[Template card type: badge + hand-lettered text, yellow blanks](../topics/text.md#l11-template-card-typography)**: A dark translucent pill badge (yellow ring number + condensed sans label, e.g. '1 Expertise Hook') with a thin rule under it, then the template typing on word by word in a casual hand-lettered font with a white glow; blanks [X] [Y] [niche] in yellow-orange with glow. Centred at ~64% height on his chest.
- **[Visual table of contents in the first 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#l11-toc-intro)**: 0–2 s: a blur-in and a 30% eased punch-out while a frosted-glass numbered list of all 7 hook names scrolls up above his head and '7HOOK' (heavy rounded red neon sans + white script 'that'll always work') sits on his chest. The viewer sees the whole menu (and the count) before the first item.

## Publish

- **[Export silent; pick a low-use track in-app](../topics/sound.md#sound-low-use-count-track)**: Khandala was exported silent and the music chosen in Edits with the use count checked (under ~10K uses is ideal); a place-name song adds nostalgia. Our early edits went out silent this way (L02).
- **[No paragraph over two lines](../topics/text.md#text-two-line-paragraphs)**: Harry hasn't written a paragraph over two lines since March 2021: short paragraphs are monkey bars, easy to swing between; shorter is better most of the time. ⚠ C9
- **[Long candid caption as a personal note](../topics/text.md#text-long-candid-caption)**: Rahul's long, candid captions read as a personal note that rewards readers ("I don't know if any of you read the caption… tell me in the comments"). ⚠ C9
- **[Caption: hook line, story, CTA, 3–5 tags](../topics/text.md#text-caption-structure)**: Line 1 = hook/keyword line visible before "more"; 1–3 lines of story or value; a CTA (send/save); 3–5 hashtags. Khandala used a Hinglish chill reel caption and an English story carousel caption.
- **[Keywords in caption and text over hashtags](../topics/text.md#text-seo-over-hashtags)**: Keyword-rich captions and on-screen text ("Khandala sunset point") over hashtags; 3–5 precise hashtags; add alt text, location tag, collaborator tags and a first-comment idea.
- **[Ask before posting faces](../topics/filming.md#film-consent-faces)**: Get a yes from everyone visible before posting or tagging; Khandala media stays outside the repo because colleagues appear in it.
- **[CTA to a landing page or email list](../topics/growth.md#growth-cta-to-owned-list)**: Every piece needs an ask, and Oren's points to an owned list: his bio CTA is "join my brand strategy newsletter". ⚠ C23, C1
- **[Short form = awareness, long = conversion](../topics/growth.md#growth-short-awareness-long-conversion)**: Short form drives awareness; long form is where conversion happens, because time spent with you raises willingness to act.
- **[2–3 platforms, one at a time](../topics/growth.md#growth-two-three-platforms)**: Prioritise 2–3 platforms to avoid single-platform risk; focus resources on one while the others sit in maintenance mode, then rotate ("Eye of Sauron").
- **[Master one network, cross-post the rest](../topics/growth.md#growth-master-one-cross-post)**: Get good at one primary network (usually Instagram) first, cross-post everywhere because it compounds, and build per-network strategies later. ⚠ C33
- **[Native beats identical cross-posting](../topics/growth.md#growth-native-over-cross-post)**: Same content everywhere hits a ceiling; give the same footage to platform-native editors: the meat stays, the hook changes per platform. ⚠ C33
- **[Collab posts bring new audiences](../topics/growth.md#growth-collab-pillar)**: A regular collaborator making about 4 collab posts a month brings a new audience; our Khandala carousel was planned as a Collab with a colleague, and tags add reach via their networks.
- **[Bio in three lines](../topics/growth.md#growth-bio-three-lines)**: Line 1 what you do, line 2 why follow, line 3 a CTA.
- **[Reply to commenters yourself](../topics/growth.md#growth-reply-personally)**: Make engagement the goal: reply to the people already commenting, yourself (even ~5 a week), reward participation, use niche inside jokes ("bulking season"); teams reply only from a labelled team account. ⚠ C16
- **[First 60 minutes after posting](../topics/growth.md#growth-first-60-minutes)**: Share to Stories with a sticker/poll (Khandala: a "Guess the point?" poll), reply to every comment, DM it to a few friends who'd enjoy it.
- **[Perfect is the enemy of posted](../topics/growth.md#growth-perfect-enemy-of-posted)**: Don't withhold posts for the audience; start with a sustainable baseline (e.g. 1 YouTube video every 2 weeks + 3 shorts a week). Briar: sometimes just post (a camera-on, step-back clip got 14,000 views). ⚠ C13, C21
- **[Accordion: volume to learn, then effort](../topics/growth.md#growth-accordion-method)**: Expand volume early to learn what the audience calls quality (3 → 5 YouTube videos a week, "just trimmed"), then compress: Feb 2025 Caleb puts five posts' effort into three. ⚠ C13, C14
- **[Expert content: 3 a week minimum](../topics/growth.md#growth-expert-cadence)**: Expert-on-camera content is "a three times a week kind of minimum"; narrative accounts about 2 a week. ⚠ C26
- **[Fast growers: no missed days, one line](../topics/growth.md#growth-tiktok-daily-ig-skip)**: Fast growers stay on one line for a year and don't miss days on TikTok; Instagram tolerates skipping a bad day. Keep a bank of 14–15 videos.
- **[Follower ads and ad-only exposure hurt](../topics/growth.md#growth-paid-followers-hurt)**: Bought followers (~$2 each) skip the first 3 s, dragging hook rate and watch time; people who only saw you in ads auto-scroll your posts.
- **[Trial Reels test hooks on non-followers](../topics/growth.md#growth-trial-reels)**: Trial Reels (once 1,000+ followers) test hooks and variations with non-followers before followers see them; Briar names them as a growth tactic without explaining.
- **[Default posting windows (IST)](../topics/growth.md#growth-posting-windows-ist)**: Weekdays 7–9 PM, lunch 12:30–2 PM, weekends 10 AM–12 PM and 6–9 PM, to be replaced by own Insights; Khandala reel planned Thu 7:30 PM, carousel Sun 8 PM.
- **[Originality: no watermarks or near-duplicates](../topics/growth.md#growth-originality)**: No reposted or watermarked clips, no near-duplicates of other creators; trends are a format to adapt, not a video to copy.
- **[Specs: 9:16 reels, 4:5 or 3:4 feed](../topics/growth.md#growth-format-specs)**: Reels 1080×1920, 30 fps (60 for slow-mo sources), HDR off unless the phone's HDR uploads well; feed/carousel 4:5 1080×1350 or the 3:4 grid crop (Khandala carousel 1080×1440).
- **[Only 9/10+ ships; walk around the garden](../topics/process.md#proc-nine-ten-standard)**: Your work is your standards: nine out of ten or it doesn't go out; it's done when nothing can be added or taken away.
- **[Lead-magnet CTA over a recap strip](../topics/growth.md#l11-lead-magnet-recap-cta)**: CTA: "If you want a list of 100 proven viral hooks just like these, comment the word hook and I'll send them to you for free", over a sideways-scrolling strip of every example clip, '100 PROVEN VIRAL HOOKS' and a glowing yellow 'HOOK'. Caption: '(No emails)'. Result at download: 5,564 comments on 8,070 likes. ⚠ C1, C23

## Analyse

- **[Keyword CTA: ~10× more comments](../topics/growth.md#growth-keyword-cta-comment-gap)**: Rahul's keyword-CTA reels got 4–26% comments per like (median ≈ 13%); his one no-CTA reel got 1.3% (88 comments on 256K plays). n = 1, but the clearest natural experiment in the sample. ⚠ C1
- **[Follower-first: ghost followers, non-follower %](../topics/growth.md#growth-follower-first-ghosts)**: New posts go to followers first; off-topic followers scroll past and stall reach. Check non-follower view % on the last 5–10 posts: above ~50% is probably fine.
- **[Viral For You = 4–5× your baseline](../topics/growth.md#growth-viral-for-you)**: Viral is relative: about 4–5× your own baseline (500 views → 2,000 is viral for you); then the baseline climbs.
- **[Multiplier sheet: score posts vs median](../topics/growth.md#growth-multiplier-sheet)**: Per platform and format, benchmark = median of the last 75–90 days; report each post as a multiple (150K ÷ 100K = 1.5×) after ~11 days; update the benchmark monthly; share across platforms.
- **[Monthly top-10% review](../topics/growth.md#growth-top-10-percent-review)**: Take the last 90 days (or 30), find the top 10% and what occurred in all of them (usually one or two things); learn from the top, not the bottom; redo monthly.
- **[Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data)**: Split each week's videos into hook (psychological principle), format (visual form), topic (one word) and illustration (metaphor, story, stat, quote); test each part separately the next week.
- **[Track only metrics that change actions](../topics/growth.md#growth-track-few-metrics)**: Track 2–4 metrics that change what you do next; optimise for conversions (sales, leads, hires) over likes. Caleb would take 30–40% fewer views for a higher conversion rate.
- **[Per-post vs account metrics](../topics/growth.md#growth-post-and-account-metrics)**: Per post: hook rate, views, saves, shares. Per account: monthly reach, leads/sign-ups/email adds, sales attributed to social. ⚠ C24
- **[Reels signals: watch time, sends, saves](../topics/growth.md#growth-ranking-signals)**: Our playbook's order for non-follower reach: watch time/completion and rewatches, sends per reach (DM shares), saves, meaningful comments, then likes.
- **[Pillar system: 3–5 formats × 3–4 a month](../topics/growth.md#growth-pillar-system)**: Test 3–5 formats, each 3–4 times a month (12–16 posts); review views, saves, shares, hook rate and new vs old followers a couple of days after month end (~1 h); swap a format after two worse months. ⚠ C26
- **[Don't benchmark a paid outlier](../topics/growth.md#growth-outlier-paid-not-benchmark)**: Rahul's 11.3M sponsored reel had 0.3% likes per play and 334 comments, 10–17× below his organic engagement: it fits paid amplification, so it isn't an organic benchmark.
- **[Brick-by-brick list of what works](../topics/process.md#proc-brick-by-brick)**: Keep an internal list of specific things that improve your content; it becomes an onboarding and training tool.
- **[Weekly update: wins, next, blockers, numbers](../topics/process.md#proc-weekly-update)**: A weekly note up the chain: wins, what's next, blockers, KPIs.
- **[Download references for local analysis](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-yt-dlp-references)**: yt-dlp downloads YouTube (Instagram often blocked) references for local study; the Rahul study downloaded 12 reels this way, for analysis only.
- **[Measure reference reels with code](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-measure-reels-pipeline)**: Our Rahul study: ffmpeg scene-cut detection, OpenCV frame-difference beats, 1 fps and 4 fps contact sheets, EBU R128 loudness, noise floor, Whisper language check.

## Monetise

- **[Weekly lead magnet into an owned list](../topics/growth.md#growth-lead-magnet-series)**: One weekly lead-magnet CTA tied to a series ("comment data for my 5-day course"); email reaches ~100% vs under half of followers seeing a reel; Substack adds discovery (Briar's claims). ⚠ C1, C18
- **[Trust before transactions](../topics/business.md#biz-trust-before-transactions)**: Give value, show credibility, build relationship before selling; let content sell (soft CTA, client results, process, objections). Educational content scales trust. Test every move: will it increase or decrease trust? ⚠ C10
- **[Share the knowledge, sell the execution](../topics/business.md#biz-share-knowledge-sell-execution)**: Give the real frameworks, "not some teaser"; people realise execution is hard and pay for it. Briar gives away "the sauce": others take months to apply it. ⚠ C11
- **[Offer ladder and five money models](../topics/business.md#biz-offer-ladder)**: Free → lead magnet → $10–100 → $500–5K → $10K+, one offer first. Models: services, products, affiliates/sponsors (only what you use), community, ads as add-on.
- **[Creator pyramid: micro, mid, anchors](../topics/business.md#biz-creator-pyramid)**: Micro creators for volume and ad creative, mid-tier (30K–100K) as the core, a few big anchors on top. Brands pay via ad creative, seeding, affiliates, paid posts and whitelisting.
- **[Whitelisting vs darklisting](../topics/business.md#biz-whitelisting)**: Whitelisting: a brand runs the creator's own post as an ad via an ad/partnership code (often outperforms). Darklisting: an ad from the creator's account that never appears on their feed.
- **[Modular brief](../topics/business.md#biz-modular-brief)**: Two key messages, target, content type, hook inspiration (text/visual/spoken), references, mechanism, simple outline, assets, variants (CTA versions, 2–3 hooks). The best 10% of creators don't need it.
- **[Ad maths and the Meta test](../topics/business.md#biz-ad-maths)**: 3:1 LTV:CAC north star; thumb stop doesn't matter if ROAS hits. Test: one concept per ad set, ~$50/day, lookalikes 3% → 10%, 3–10 distinct ads, spend 3–5× target CPA before judging. ⚠ C24
- **[Closer to the dollars, more money](../topics/business.md#biz-closer-to-dollars)**: Funnel: attention → CTA → landing page → lead/sale → CRM → fast touches. A landing page removes every buying objection. North stars: page conversion and close rate.
- **[Email 1–3 a week, plain text](../topics/business.md#biz-email-cadence)**: Campaigns vs automated flows; 1–3 sends a week, plain text from a person (Oren). Harry: less news, more letter: time-and-place intro, 5–6 examples with conflict, no paragraph over two lines.
- **[Follow up with "not now" people](../topics/business.md#biz-follow-up-not-now)**: Content is a mini follow-up; funnel = calls × show × close + follow-up closes. Their example: 100K views → $175K/month, $536K with better follow-up (unverified). Lowercase "quick question" email.
- **[Ads work better with organic presence](../topics/business.md#biz-ads-need-organic)**: Paid ads without an organic presence give poor return; closers close 10–15% higher when the prospect can see your content (claim).
- **[Copy is the number-one marketing skill](../topics/business.md#biz-copywriting-top-skill)**: Same product, different words: Snickers vs Fuse. Lifting landing-page conversion from 1% to 2% doubles growth.
- **[Team: bottleneck hires, platform owners](../topics/business.md#biz-team-hire-bottleneck)**: Hire for the bottleneck; platform specialists over a generalist manager; culture over skills. Platform owners split 85% primary / 15% secondary. Contractors in year 0–1, core roles in-house by years 1–3.

## Mindset

- **[Quality is defined by the audience](../topics/filming.md#film-quality-audience-defined)**: The audience decides what quality is, not the creator or the gear; some of the most viral videos are shot at night on a phone. ⚠ C13
- **[Growth timelines and 1% maths (claims)](../topics/growth.md#growth-one-percent-better)**: Briar: 300 views + 1% a day ≈ 11,400 average views in a year. Oren: traction in 3–5 months of a pillar system. Caleb: 2–3 months of consistency = "top 1%". All their estimates.
- **[AI is only as good as your taste](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-only-as-good-as-taste)**: Harry: AI is a tool and predictive; taste, conviction and first-hand experience are what it can't supply; it's a great research tool. ⚠ C8
- **[Be excited; light people up](../topics/process.md#mind-light-people-up)**: Be excited and have fun or it won't do well. People want to hear from someone at their level or one above; nobody is too old or too niche.
- **[Confidence comes from evidence](../topics/process.md#mind-confidence-from-evidence)**: Confidence comes from evidence, evidence from effort. Niches make saturation not real: maybe three in a thousand actually put in the work.
- **[Results over ego](../topics/process.md#mind-results-over-ego)**: Don't let insecurity stop you posting; look at the metrics. Iteration over perfection: comfort doesn't build iconic brands. If friends on Instagram make you nervous, start on TikTok.
- **[Silence and action](../topics/process.md#mind-silence-and-action)**: Harry avoids phone-first mornings (they make the day "drudge"), takes silent walks with no earphones and silent writing retreats.
- **[Mentorship = speed](../topics/process.md#mind-mentorship-speed)**: Work for them or pay them, and ask short, specific questions; Briar spent 80% of his time for 20% of his income to learn in an agency.

## Gym extras

- **[Gym: wrong vs right split-screen tip](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-gym-wrong-vs-right)** (idea): Single-exercise tip shown as wrong vs right in a split-screen; high save rate.
- **[Gym formats to rotate](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-gym-rotation-formats)** (idea): Rotate: "Chest day in 30 seconds" vlog (B-roll + 3–4 exercises with sets×reps on screen), "3 exercises for [muscle]" list, monthly progress series (same angle and light), gym humour/POV, diary voice-over, high-protein Indian meals.
- **[Speed ramps: dead time, beats, top rep](../topics/editing.md#edit-speed-ramps)** (edit): Subtle ramps on browser scrolls and screen recordings remove dead time (L07); the L08 teaser syncs ramps to percussive hits; our gym default ramps into the top rep.
- **[Cut on the beat or on motion](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-on-beat-motion)** (edit): Our edit blueprint sets cut rules (on the beat or on motion) and travel uses a wide → close-up rhythm. Khandala cut every 1.5 s, which lands on 80 and 120 BPM beats (2 or 3 beats per shot), so music could be added later.
- **[Trending audio only when it fits](../topics/sound.md#sound-trending-audio-fit)** (sound): Trending audio boosts discovery when it fits the format: energetic for gym transformations, nostalgic acoustic for travel recaps, spoken for skits; original voice-over builds connection.
- **[Animated number counters](../topics/effects.md#fx-number-counter)** (graphics): Numbers count up on screen (5,220,123 sounds, GitHub stars ticking; Rahul's odometer ₹ counter and an opening price ticker counting to ₹75,000).
- **[Gym grade: cool, contrasty, textured](../topics/colour.md#colour-gym-grade)** (edit): Slightly cooler or neutral, higher contrast, clarity/texture up for muscle definition, shadows lifted only a little, distracting signage colours desaturated, subtle vignette.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)** (edit): Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **[iPhone 15: frame rates, modes, HDR](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-frame-rates)** (film): 4K 30 default; 4K 60 for reps you'll slow; 4K 24 for travel; 240 fps slo-mo for single moments; Action mode handheld; Cinematic mode for B-roll; HDR Video off for heavy grading (no Log/ProRes on the base 15).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)** (film): The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Gym filming: etiquette and side light](../topics/filming.md#film-gym-side-light)** (film): Never film others without consent, don't hog kit, keep the tripod out of walkways; avoid windows and mirrors and let overhead light hit the muscle from the side; film when quieter.
- **[Tripod height changes the story](../topics/filming.md#film-tripod-heights)** (film): Low (41–60 cm) makes lifts look powerful; chest height is neutral; high (120–133 cm, tilted 10–20°) shows symmetry. A light tripod: thickest legs first, column down, legs spread, bag hung on it, out of plate paths.
- **[Solo: record, then walk in](../topics/filming.md#film-solo-start)** (film): Start recording and walk into frame (trim later), or use the 3 s/10 s timer; a watch or Bluetooth remote is faster.
- **[Gym B-roll every session](../topics/filming.md#film-gym-broll)** (film): Walking in, chalk/straps, loading plates, headphones on, pre-workout scoop, pump close-ups, rerack, water sip, mirror check, logging the set.
- **[Two angles per exercise](../topics/filming.md#film-two-angles)** (film): Move the tripod between sets to shoot each exercise from two angles so the edit can cut between them.
- **[Gym angles: chest, shoulders, arms, abs](../topics/filming.md#film-angles-chest)** (film): Bench 45° from the foot end at bench height; presses front 45° slightly low; lateral raises from behind; rear delts top-down; arms side-front close-ups and slow-mo last reps; hanging abs in side profile, floor abs top-down.
- **[Gym angles: legs and back](../topics/filming.md#film-angles-legs)** (film): Squats side-on at hip height; quads low front 45°; RDL from behind; lats from directly behind and slightly low; V-taper high-behind; rows and deadlifts in side profile.
- **[Reply to commenters yourself](../topics/growth.md#growth-reply-personally)** (publish): Make engagement the goal: reply to the people already commenting, yourself (even ~5 a week), reward participation, use niche inside jokes ("bulking season"); teams reply only from a labelled team account.
- **[Seven-repo editing stack](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-seven-tool-stack)** (edit): FFmpeg (every cut, mix, render), faster-whisper (word timing), Whisper, yt-dlp (download sources), OpenCV + contrib CSRT tracker (follow the speaker in a 9:16 crop), Puppeteer (render HTML captions), HyperFrames (agent-built motion graphics).
- **[Before/after slider reveals the grade](../topics/effects.md#l10-grade-slider-reveal)** (edit): The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.
- **[Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook)** (script): Template: "If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]". A tiny repeatable habit, 'every single day', then three concrete outcomes (rule of three). Each outcome is another reason to care. Reel's example: "If you take creatine every single day, you're going to build more muscle, recover faster, and get way more out of all the hard work that you're putting in in the gym" (pill 28M, the reel's biggest example).
- 🔥 Trend: **The Great Lock In 2026 / #winterarc (Sep 1 to Dec 31)** (heat 4/5): Self-improvement push for the last four months of the year: declarations of rules and routines, discipline montages, early-morning gym, check-ins. In 2026 it is more holistic (sleep, money, mental health). Runs until Dec 31, so it still has two months of life.
