- 🔥 Trend: **Strava-style stats overlay POV (pace, reps, heart rate on screen)** (heat 3/5): POV workout or run footage with live stat overlays (distance, pace, HR, map, or reps and kg). Lightreel lists 'Strava-style edits' as a rising format. Most creators use CapCut templates.

## Tech extras

- **[No intro: topic and number first](../topics/hooks.md#hook-no-intro-payoff-first)** (script): Rahul never greets: the topic and a number (price, score, date) are spoken and on screen in the first 1–2 s. Our playbook: open on the most striking frame plus a hook text of 8 words or fewer; no logos, no slow intros.
- **[Contrarian statement or "don't buy X"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrarian-statement)** (script): Say something most people believe is false and offer the alternative ("Subscribers, views, likes don't matter…"). Rahul's versions: "Don't buy the RTX 5070", "8 GB GPU in 2026 is a waste of money", "stop paying ₹8,000 a year for Photoshop".
- **[Verdict first: name, price, score](../topics/hooks.md#hook-verdict-first)** (script): Rating reels open on the product, its price and an x/10 verdict in the first second, then a one-word justification label ("Core i9 14900K, ₹46,000, 3 out of 10… as hot as a heater").
- **["Do this now": a tiny effort, instant payoff](../topics/hooks.md#hook-do-this-now)** (script): The viewer can test it while watching: "put your phone on airplane mode… the code is still changing", or "Aapko pata hai…" change one word in the Gmail URL. The Gmail trick was Rahul's best organic reel at 2.38× followers.
- **[Hyper-local conditional hook](../topics/hooks.md#hook-hyper-local-conditional)** (script): Call out a specific place and moment: "If you're going to Nehru Place or Lamington Road this weekend to build a PC, listen before you enter the shop…", with real market names as road-sign graphics.
- **[Sarcastic or date-stamped mockery opener](../topics/hooks.md#hook-sarcastic-opener)** (script): Open with mockery tied to a date or price ("Thinking of a ₹1 lakh PC in October 2026? The shopkeeper will laugh at you") or sarcastic congratulations ("Wow, congratulations! ₹75,000… your first PC").
- **[Study one same-niche creator deeply](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-study-one-creator-deeply)** (analyse): Our Rahul file benchmarks one same-niche creator in depth: 12 reels downloaded and measured (cuts, beats, loudness, hooks, CTAs).
- **[Universal tricks reach, niche builds engage](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-universal-vs-niche-reach)** (analyse): In Rahul's sample, universal everyday-tech tricks (Gmail, 2.38× followers) got the most non-follower reach; PC-build reels got the highest like rates (4.8–5.3%); AI "debunk" content was weakest.
- **[Split layouts: graphic plus face](../topics/editing.md#edit-split-screen-graphic-face)** (edit): Graphic on top, face below, switching to full face for key lines (L01); Rahul's animated top ~55% over a face cam; L04's red step board under the face; long-form: 9:16 examples in rounded windows on the left ~40%, speaker on the right (L06).
- **[Switch layouts every few seconds](../topics/editing.md#edit-layout-switching)** (edit): Rahul's organic reels switch between full-frame talking head with pop-up labels, screen/card with circular face cam, and 1–3 s meme cutaways every few seconds instead of holding one layout.
- **[Screen content with a circular face cam](../topics/editing.md#edit-screen-card-circle-facecam)** (edit): Screen recordings fill the frame with a circular face cam: Rahul bottom-centre with a yellow ring and an app-logo badge; Oren in dark rounded cards with drop shadows plus a floating circular PiP camera.
- **[Meme cutaways with the product pasted in](../topics/editing.md#edit-meme-cutaways)** (edit): 1–3 s full-screen meme cutaways (Bollywood, Joker, DiCaprio, Messi) with the price or product composited in; often reused as the cover.
- **[Show proof on screen](../topics/editing.md#edit-proof-inserts)** (edit): Rahul inserts article, doc and GitHub screenshots with yellow highlighter on the key line; Oren runs live tool walkthroughs as proof.
- **[Keyboard clicks and UI pops on bullets](../topics/sound.md#sound-ui-clicks-bullets)** (sound): UI clicks on screen recordings (L06); mechanical keyboard clicks, UI bubble pops and switch clicks on bullets and badges (L07).
- **[Mix measured at −14 LUFS](../topics/sound.md#sound-loudness-minus-14)** (sound): All 12 Rahul reels measured −14 LUFS with a 2.2–4.8 LU range (heavily compressed). The quietest 5% sits 9–21 dB under speech, never silent, pointing to a constant low bed (inferred).
- **[Voice-led, no trending audio](../topics/sound.md#sound-voice-led-no-trending)** (sound): None of Rahul's 12 reels lists a music track; the voice dominates throughout.
- **[Animated number counters](../topics/effects.md#fx-number-counter)** (graphics): Numbers count up on screen (5,220,123 sounds, GitHub stars ticking; Rahul's odometer ₹ counter and an opening price ticker counting to ₹75,000).
- **[Frosted cards, drawn diagrams, red arrows](../topics/effects.md#fx-frosted-glass-cards)** (graphics): Frosted-glass UI cards (L01, L02), drawn diagrams (curves, radar, fishing line) and red circles/arrows that guide the eye (L01).
- **[B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline)** (edit): Desaturate and hold the frame on a sarcastic line.
- **[Price strikes, stamps, pills and ticks](../topics/effects.md#fx-price-strike-through)** (graphics): Strike through the old price then show the new; a red "DON'T BUY" stamp; green "₹60,000 SAVED" and "FREE" pills; ticks filling a checklist.
- **[Live-build parts card with budget bar](../topics/effects.md#fx-live-build-parts-card)** (graphics): An empty parts grid fills slot by slot with names and prices while a progress bar shows budget used; a date stamp anchors it.
- **[TV colour-bar glitch transition](../topics/transitions.md#tr-glitch-colour-bars)** (edit): A TV colour-bar "glitch" transition appears in two of Rahul's reels.
- **[Teaching text: clean sans, red/green](../topics/text.md#text-clean-sans-teaching)** (graphics): Clean sans (Inter / SF Pro style), white and yellow on dark; red = bad/wrong (or price up), green = good/right (or saved).
- **[Extended bold sans titles, neon highlights](../topics/text.md#text-extended-sans-neon)** (graphics): Extended bold geometric sans titles (Druk Wide / Monument Extended style) + Inter/Neue Haas body; white on dark with cyan, lime and neon-pink highlights on numbers and acronyms.
- **[Yellow caps labels and big ₹ figures](../topics/text.md#text-yellow-condensed-labels)** (graphics): Heavy condensed all-caps yellow labels of 1–3 words on a black box ("WI-FI OFF"), large yellow ₹ figures with a drop shadow, and receipt-style or dark UI data cards that look like real documents.
- **[Date-stamped prices](../topics/text.md#text-date-stamped-prices)** (graphics): "10 OCT 2026" stamps, dated retailer tags and "was ₹X on 10th, now ₹Y" anchor each claim in time.
- **[Long candid caption as a personal note](../topics/text.md#text-long-candid-caption)** (publish): Rahul's long, candid captions read as a personal note that rewards readers ("I don't know if any of you read the caption… tell me in the comments").
- **[Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known)** (script): Make a product make sense by comparing it to products people know: "Tougher than an F-150, faster than a 911" (concrete word, shorter, parallel).
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)** (script): Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Covers: payoff frame, number, face, accent](../topics/text.md#text-cover-meme-payoff)** (graphics): Rahul's meme covers come from the reel's own payoff frame, so the cover promises the ending; covers carry a ₹ number or score, a face and yellow accent. Our playbook keeps one cover style per pillar.
- **[Near-black with one accent colour](../topics/colour.md#colour-near-black-one-accent)** (graphics): The easing tutorial is near-black with a red glow, red as the only accent; Rahul uses yellow (≈ #F5B800) on black as his single brand accent everywhere.
- **[Fixed set and colour identity](../topics/brand.md#brand-fixed-set-identity)** (film): Rahul's set never changes (purple/blue wash, warm lamp, mic on an arm) with a yellow accent; he talks straight to lens, sarcastic ("Come on Intel") with lots of gestures, recognisable at thumbnail size.
- **[Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta)** (script): "Comment 'hooks' and I'll send it to you": a comment-to-DM freebie, with social proof (700K views) raising its value. Rahul uses it on nearly every reel with the keyword in the caption and as a big yellow label in the last 2–4 s.
- **[Keyword CTA: ~10× more comments](../topics/growth.md#growth-keyword-cta-comment-gap)** (analyse): Rahul's keyword-CTA reels got 4–26% comments per like (median ≈ 13%); his one no-CTA reel got 1.3% (88 comments on 256K plays). n = 1, but the clearest natural experiment in the sample.
- **[Show the comment → DM funnel on screen](../topics/growth.md#growth-show-the-funnel)** (graphics): The ending shows a mock comment box with the keyword being typed, then a DM preview with the freebie; Rahul's freebies are living resources (live-price part lists, tier list, checklist), not a repeat of the video.
- **[Withhold the rest: "comment for the rest"](../topics/growth.md#growth-withheld-remainder)** (script): CPU Ratings shows only 6 CPUs, flashes the full tier list at the end and says "Comment CPU for the rest".
- **[Monthly franchise and a running storyline](../topics/growth.md#growth-monthly-franchise)** (idea): "₹X PC Build – October 2026" labels make refreshable monthly franchises; a repeated storyline ("prices rising weekly, we're cooked") gives each reel a reason to exist this week.
- **[Rahul: ~1 reel a day, two time slots](../topics/growth.md#growth-rahul-cadence)** (publish): 10 reels in 10 days with double posts on two days, mostly at 10:00–11:30 or 17:30–19:30 IST; the two pinned slots hold sponsored reels.
- **[Don't benchmark a paid outlier](../topics/growth.md#growth-outlier-paid-not-benchmark)** (analyse): Rahul's 11.3M sponsored reel had 0.3% likes per play and 334 comments, 10–17× below his organic engagement: it fits paid amplification, so it isn't an organic benchmark.
- **[Sponsor as the "pro" answer](../topics/business.md#biz-sponsor-as-smart-option)** (monetise): Build the sponsor into a comparison (dumb → normal → pro streamer) so the product is the pro answer, not an interruption.
- **[Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown)** (idea): Play another creator's popular or paid reel with its audio in a rounded card. Freeze it at each effect, shrink it to a thumbnail beside your head, explain how to make that effect, then play on. In L10 the source plays 10 times, 19.9 s of 85 s (23%), and its own lines carry the story.
- **[Undercut a paid course in the hook](../topics/hooks.md#l10-undercut-paid-hook)** (script): Open with the rival's strongest line ("I didn't edit a single second of this video. Claude did."), then undercut its price: "This guy's selling this for 97 bucks. I'm giving it away for free." A $97 checkout card pops on the source as he says it.
- **[Demo each effect on your own shot](../topics/effects.md#l10-apply-effect-on-yourself)** (edit): Each technique is applied to his own footage as he names it: grade-panel sliders move and his saturation measurably drops (SATAVG ~8 to ~4.5 at 56 s), his shot shrinks into the centre of the 3x3 wall, the words go behind his head. It works as proof and as a pattern interrupt.
- **[Type the real prompt on screen](../topics/text.md#l10-prompt-bar-on-screen)** (graphics): The exact prompt types on in a dark rounded chat bar with an orange send button (Claude-app look), top-centre above the head. Five full prompts are shown, so the viewer can screenshot them. Claude drew the bars as vector graphics.
- **[Real screenshot beats an AI mock-up](../topics/editing.md#l10-real-screenshot-not-mockup)** (graphics): For UI graphics such as an editor timeline, a real screenshot looks better than a generated mock-up. He shows both, back to back.
- **[Tool card lands on the word](../topics/text.md#l10-card-on-the-word)** (graphics): GitHub repo cards (openai/whisper, yt-dlp) and logo cards (FFmpeg) appear exactly when the tool is named, timed from Whisper word timestamps. The caption: captions, tool labels and repo cards "land exactly when I say them".
- **[Moody grade: highlights down, blacks up](../topics/colour.md#l10-moody-grade-recipe)** (edit): His recommended look: curves pull the highlights down and lift the blacks, saturation down 15%, then a soft vignette. On-screen panel values: Highlights -35, Blacks +12, Saturation -15, Vignette -40. His own footage sits at mean luma ~25-28% with very low saturation and warm practical lamps.
- **[3x3 wall of reels proves a trend](../topics/effects.md#l10-3x3-reel-wall)** (graphics): To show that "lots of people are doing this", his shot shrinks into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid and 8 downloaded reels pop in around it, one per frame. The grid then stays on as the thumbnail.
- **[Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook)** (script): Template: "If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]". A tiny repeatable habit, 'every single day', then three concrete outcomes (rule of three). Each outcome is another reason to care. Reel's example: "If you take creatine every single day, you're going to build more muscle, recover faster, and get way more out of all the hard work that you're putting in in the gym" (pill 28M, the reel's biggest example).
- 🔥 Trend: **iPhone Duo launch cycle: durability, crease, 'is flopping', India price shock** (heat 5/5): Apple's first foldable (announced Sep 9, sale Oct 23; India from Rs 2,99,900). The US Science & Tech trending list on Oct 27 is dominated by it: durability destruction, crease tests and 'fixes', 'it's flopping', 'Apple is cooked', camera critiques. Indian channels react to the price.
- 🔥 Trend: **Paired versus Shorts ('6 ways A beats B', then the mirror video)** (heat 4/5): A numbered comparison Short followed two days later by the mirror version from the other side. Both halves go viral and the comments fight. Mrwhosetheboss posted 'iPhone Duo beats Samsung' (Oct 21) and 'Samsung Fold beats iPhone Duo' (Oct 23).
- 🔥 Trend: **Native-interface / finished-output-first AI and app tutorial with comment keyword** (heat 4/5): Screen recordings of ChatGPT, camera apps, CapCut or Instagram's own editor, shown live. The finished result comes first, then the steps, then 'Comment WORD and I'll DM the prompt'. The comment count can be two-thirds of the like count.
- 🔥 Trend: **PC build by budget during the RAM price crisis** (heat 4/5): Budget-tier builds (Rs 75K / 1L / 1.5L / 2L) labelled with the month, now framed against record DDR5 prices: 32GB kits around $450 in the US on Oct 14 and around Rs 40-42K in India in August. Spin-offs: 'building a PC in 2026', nostalgia rebuilds of an old PC, prebuilt-vs-DIY.
- 🔥 Trend: **Indian festive sale deal reels (Flipkart Big Bang Diwali Sale from Oct 28)** (heat 4/5): 'Impossible deals' and 'buy or skip' reels during the Diwali sales (iPhone 17 cut to about Rs 77,999 in the Big Billion Days, per DesiDime). Brands sponsor these, and they reach far beyond followers.
- 🔥 Trend: **'Your PC just...' tech-news explainer Shorts** (heat 3/5): Fast explainers on a scary-sounding news item that affects viewers' own devices. Example: the Windows Secure Boot certificate that expired on Oct 19. Also 'Microsoft buying out 60,000 employees'.

## Travel extras

- **[Hyper-local conditional hook](../topics/hooks.md#hook-hyper-local-conditional)** (script): Call out a specific place and moment: "If you're going to Nehru Place or Lamington Road this weekend to build a PC, listen before you enter the shop…", with real market names as road-sign graphics.
- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)** (script): Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story)** (idea): Oren's five: strong take, strong take → education, small epiphany ("Do you notice how husbands always do this?"), humour (poke fun at something), story time. Takes, small epiphanies and story time are the foundation of ~90% of content.
- **[Even "here's three things" beats no frame](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-any-framework-beats-none)** (idea): Tristan: even a cringey "here's three things" does better than no framework; Briar lists "9 travel hacks" as a valid reach post while calling it "kind of cringe".
- **[Travel formats: vibe, dump, POV, "nobody tells you"](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-travel-formats)** (idea): Options: 10–12 s sunset vibe reel, camera-roll dump with text, "POV: your office trip actually turns out fun", "things nobody tells you about [place]" (saveable), scrapbook carousel with location labels, 30–45 s day-in-the-trip vlog.
- **[Office-trip content gets sent to colleagues](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-workplace-trip-shareable)** (idea): Workplace-trip content is highly shareable because people DM it to colleagues ("we need this trip"); the Khandala caption CTA asks to send it to the colleague who always says "next time".
- **[Name the exact spot everywhere](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-place-specific-seo)** (publish): Use the place plus the exact viewpoint in on-screen text, caption and location tag ("Khandala Lonavala" pairs well since people search both).
- **[Cut on the beat or on motion](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-on-beat-motion)** (edit): Our edit blueprint sets cut rules (on the beat or on motion) and travel uses a wide → close-up rhythm. Khandala cut every 1.5 s, which lands on 80 and 120 BPM beats (2 or 3 beats per shot), so music could be added later.
- **[Cull near-duplicates; keep the strongest](../topics/editing.md#edit-cull-near-duplicates)** (edit): Khandala: 43 raw files to 1 reel + 1 carousel; dropped near-duplicates, tilted horizons, soft digital zooms, litter in frame and harsh midday light that broke the sunset look.
- **[Trending audio only when it fits](../topics/sound.md#sound-trending-audio-fit)** (sound): Trending audio boosts discovery when it fits the format: energetic for gym transformations, nostalgic acoustic for travel recaps, spoken for skits; original voice-over builds connection.
- **[Export silent; pick a low-use track in-app](../topics/sound.md#sound-low-use-count-track)** (publish): Khandala was exported silent and the music chosen in Edits with the use count checked (under ~10K uses is ideal); a place-name song adds nostalgia. Our early edits went out silent this way (L02).
- **[Serif italic emphasis + sans body](../topics/text.md#text-serif-italic-emphasis)** (graphics): Emphasis words in serif italic (*pro*, *honest*), body in clean sans, keyword highlights in yellow/orange. Our Khandala reel used Instrument Serif Italic.
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)** (script): Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Golden-hour travel grade](../topics/colour.md#colour-golden-hour-grade)** (edit): Warm temperature, lifted shadows, highlights pulled to keep the sun's disc, richer oranges/yellows, sky blues nudged to teal, light grain; don't oversaturate greens.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)** (edit): Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **[iPhone 15: frame rates, modes, HDR](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-frame-rates)** (film): 4K 30 default; 4K 60 for reps you'll slow; 4K 24 for travel; 240 fps slo-mo for single moments; Action mode handheld; Cinematic mode for B-roll; HDR Video off for heavy grading (no Log/ProRes on the base 15).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)** (film): The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Travel shots: silhouettes, backs, slow-mo](../topics/filming.md#film-travel-shots)** (film): Silhouettes against the sunset, group walking shots from behind, slow-motion hair/wind moments, wide → close-up rhythm.
- **[Ask before posting faces](../topics/filming.md#film-consent-faces)** (publish): Get a yes from everyone visible before posting or tagging; Khandala media stays outside the repo because colleagues appear in it.
- **[First 60 minutes after posting](../topics/growth.md#growth-first-60-minutes)** (publish): Share to Stories with a sticker/poll (Khandala: a "Guess the point?" poll), reply to every comment, DM it to a few friends who'd enjoy it.
- **[Moody grade: highlights down, blacks up](../topics/colour.md#l10-moody-grade-recipe)** (edit): His recommended look: curves pull the highlights down and lift the blacks, saturation down 15%, then a soft vignette. On-screen panel values: Highlights -35, Blacks +12, Saturation -15, Vignette -40. His own footage sits at mean luma ~25-28% with very low saturation and warm practical lamps.
- **[Before/after slider reveals the grade](../topics/effects.md#l10-grade-slider-reveal)** (edit): The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.
